To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the critical state of a thin superconductor can be treated as a mixed boundary condition, that the Erdélyy–Kober operator is the best tool for the analysis of such a mixed boundary condition and that the Erdéliy-Kober operator is a powerful mathematical tool that allows the solution of many problems of thin superconducting structures.

(i) the critical state in thin type-II superconductors can be described by a mixed boundary value condition for the magnetic field; (ii) the Erdélyy–Kober operators can be used to solve the mixed boundary value problems for the magnetic field, and (iii) the solution of the mixed boundary value problem is a generalization of the solution of the Dirichlet problem for the Laplace equation in a circular domain.

the magnetic field and critical current density distributions in thin discs and tapes can be found analytically, and the solution is given in terms of Erdélyi-Kober operators and their composition properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mathematical description of the magnetic behavior of thin superconductive samples subjected to a uniform applied magnetic field.
the development of a unified method to solve the mixed boundary value problems that arise from the critical states of superconductors in the thin limit.
the development and implementation of a method for the analytical determination of the electromagnetic field and the current density in superconducting thin strips and tapes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the method proposed here, which is based on the use of the Erdelyi–Kober operator, allows to solve a large number of problems related to superconductors, with the only requirement that the boundary conditions can be expressed in terms of mixed conditions.

the ErdélyI–Kober operators, together with the Hankel transforms, are the key tools to solve a large number of problems of the electromagnetic behavior of superconductors, and in particular of thin films, by reducing the mixed boundary value problem to the solution of a system of linear ordinary differential equations.

the operator technique is a very powerful tool that allows us to solve the mixed boundary value problem for the critical state in thin films and to extend the solution to many other more complicated cases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the critical state regime, we have provided a unified method to solve all the possible mixed boundary value problems, which are related to the electromagnetic field behavior in thin superconducting structures.
we have shown that all problems related to the critical state in thin films are reduced to finding weight functions for the Hankel transform.
we provide a general method to solve the critical state problem for thin superconductors with arbitrary boundary conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Erdélyy–Kober operators can be used to solve many different boundary value problems in the field of superconductivity.
the operator technique is a simple and effective tool to solve the critical state problems in superconducting thin structures.

the operator technique is a powerful tool to solve a large variety of mixed boundary value problems in superconducting thin films, and that the Erdélyy–Kober operators can be used in this context to obtain analytical solutions for the field and critical state distributions in thin superconducting discs and tapes.
